improvements: The bot distinguishes exhausted optional exploration from safety and preparation blockages before attempting a fallback descent.

For partly observed red-sentry rooms, the bot can scout from ordinary ground before reconsidering preparation. Fresh observations are still required before testing potions or entering hazardous flooring.
incoming_learnings: Do not reward a just-left escape door as a new withdrawal destination. Keep route protection, remembered-threat checks and mandatory key collection intact; validate actual progress after any changed withdrawal rather than assuming a safe escape.

review.review: The hero remained alive at 48/50 HP. The terminal failure was mandatory entrance-shop search exhaustion, not an observed death (decision 2686, lines 7805–7806). A separate, directly evidenced bookkeeping defect appears earlier: decision 2540 reaches branch target 944, with an explicit accepted arrival receipt at line 7384. Corridor search then preempts shopping at decisions 2541–2544. Decisions 2545–2547 still attribute three more shop inputs to that already reached target (lines 7396–7404). The search commitment survives arrival because tools/objective_planning.py:observe increments progress but originally never releases it; tools/shop_tactics.py:visit_entrance_shop subsequently resumes the stale commitment before selecting fresh work. The proposed narrow correction releases only the matching travel target on accepted arrival. It does not certify a shop visit, door inspection, loot collection or safe alternative route, and retains the 80-input bound and terminal stuck outcome. The new deterministic public-evidence fixture fails its arrival assertion on original source and passes on the candidate; all 2093 Python tests pass, with four skips. This establishes a receipt repair, not successful shop discovery or prevention of the terminal failure. Returning along that dead-end corridor may still be necessary; these three movements are not proven avoidable. The initiating terminal problem is a mandatory shop search whose admitted traversal exhausts its global allowance before remaining entrance branches are checked. Separately, decision 1531 records unresolved piranha-chest preparation (line 4513); fallback crosses to the next floor at decision 1578 (line 4722), without chest collection credit. That earlier high-priority incident remains unresolved by this focused change.
review.learnings: Release a travel commitment when its matching accepted arrival is observed, even if another controller immediately takes over. Keep arrival separate from shop visitation, hazard admission and collection. Receipt repair does not prove the store or piranha chest will be reached.

recommendations.reason: The arrival receipt patch does not establish a repair for the search envelope. Public observations do not identify which remaining unopened branch contains the store, and no alternative branch order or complete admitted itinerary has been validated within the existing allowance. Changing the limit, skipping the store, or reclassifying this as abandonable navigation would mask the failure. Next reconstruct through the first entrance-component expansion, derive its observed door/frontier graph and interrupted key-detour costs, and test a rooted, remaining-budget-aware itinerary on copies with existing route and fresh-arrival checks. Do not feed later recorded observations after any changed selection.

recommendations.reason: Unaddressed by the single arrival-bookkeeping correction. The concrete safety gap is a protected identification-and-chest-return transaction: unidentified colors do not establish invisibility, and the incident supplies no admitted trial bank with carried-potion collateral protection and a duration-funded return. Next derive paired first-pool and incident fixtures from the public terrain and selecting bookkeeping, then validate fresh bank/stash admission, actual protection duration, interruption recovery and accepted chest pickup. Do not guess potion effects, waive the chest or treat fallback descent as collection.
